correctness.rationale: Recomputed imaginary-root equation: sin(theta)+sin(2theta)=sin(theta)(1+2cos(theta))=0. All positive crossings consist of theta=2k*pi at omega=sqrt(a-b), odd pi at omega=sqrt(a), and 2pi/3 or 4pi/3 mod 2pi at omega=sqrt(a+b/2). Since 0<b<a, the first three times are T1=2pi/(3gamma), T2=pi/sqrt(a), T3=4pi/(3gamma). Checked inequalities against next 2pi/sqrt(a-b), 3pi/sqrt(a), 8pi/(3gamma). At crossings implicit derivative inverse has real part -4Re[1/(bS(theta))] and sign of crossing equals -sign(cos theta+2cos2theta), hence +,-,+ as claimed, each simple. At tau=0 simple ±i sqrt(a-b) roots shift left at derivative -3b/4, all right-half-plane roots bounded |s|²<=a+b. Root count is 0,2,0,2 successively, giving the two stable windows. Single-delay crossing interlacing for b>5a/13 gives no return to zero count. Theta model parameter substitution cited in source yields a=4,b=2, conditional on its stated characteristic coefficients; independently checked three spectral roots and directions, not model-wide nonlinear theory.
